members.name: persuasion_v7b
members.instructions: A persuader is chatting with a persuadee to convince them to donate to the charity Save the Children. Classify ONLY the final persuader message (after 'Persuader message to tag'), using the earlier dialogue only as context for what the message is replying to. Choose the persuasion strategy or dialogue act the message performs.

criteria.greeting_open: Says hello or opens the chat with a social greeting or a 'how are you' check-in.
criteria.greeting_reply_state: Replies to the partner's 'how are you' with the persuader's own wellbeing (fine, good, doing well), as part of the opening exchange.
criteria.closing_wrapup: Wraps up or ends the chat without thanking: says goodbye, wishes the partner a nice day, says the conversation is done.
criteria.confirm_or_clarify: Confirms or double-checks an amount or decision the persuadee already stated, or clarifies/corrects something the persuader said, without any persuasion.
criteria.plain_answer: A bare answer to the persuadee's question (yes, no, not sure, I don't know) that carries no persuasion strategy or information.
criteria.thank: Thanks the partner (for their time, for chatting, for donating, for a kind word), possibly together with a farewell.
criteria.acknowledge_backchannel: A short acknowledgement or agreement with what the partner just said: ok, I see, I understand, I agree, right, me too, true, indeed.
criteria.praise_user: Compliments the persuadee as a person: their kindness, generosity, decision to donate, or character.
criteria.ask_know_org: Asks whether the persuadee has heard of, knows about, or is familiar with Save the Children or what it does.
criteria.ask_personal_experience: A question about the persuadee's own charity-relevant life, habits or experience: whether they donate to charities, how often, to which ones, whether they have children, whether they volunteer, how they spend their money, their personal views on helping others. Includes pointed or rhetorical questions about the persuadee's own habits used to persuade.
criteria.ask_task_opinion: Asks the persuadee's opinion, feelings, or interest about this charity, the cause, or donating to it (what do you think, would you like to know more, do you have questions, does this concern you).
criteria.off_task_chat: Small talk unrelated to charity or donating: where the persuadee lives, hobbies, weather, jobs, the survey/HIT mechanics, or other topics.
criteria.org_mission_description: Describes what Save the Children is, does, or has already achieved: its mission, programs, regions where it works, history, founder, partnerships, and the results it has had for children and families, as factual information about the organization.
criteria.org_trust_reputation: Argues the charity is trustworthy or reputable: ratings, share of funds going to programs, accountability, longevity, where to verify it (website), celebrity or official backing.
criteria.emotion_suffering: Facts or statistics about children's suffering (children dying, injured in war, hungry, separated from families, living in poverty), which evoke sympathy.
criteria.emotion_feelings_guilt: A statement that expresses or elicits emotion directly: sadness, heartbreak, guilt, hope, how good it will feel to help, the children need you; or contrasts our own comfort and privilege with what others lack.
criteria.logical_reasoning: Gives a reason or argument why the persuadee donating makes sense: the impact the persuadee's donation would have, how money helps, that children deserve a chance, that we can afford it, cause and effect.
criteria.small_amount_foot_in_door: Pushes toward a small donation or minimal first step: even a small amount or a few cents helps, every little bit counts, suggests a small specific amount.
criteria.donation_procedure: Gives practical information about the donation: what this chat is about when the persuadee is unsure (that it concerns a donation to the charity), without itself asking them to give, that it is deducted from the task payment, that any amount in the range or whatever the persuadee is comfortable with is fine, that the research team will send it, how and when to pay.
criteria.propose_donation: Asks or invites the persuadee to donate (would you donate some of your payment, will you consider giving), without asking for a specific amount.
criteria.ask_amount: Asks the persuadee how much they would like to donate.
criteria.self_modeling: States that the persuader donates, regularly gives, or will donate, or offers to match, setting an example for the persuadee.
criteria.personal_story: Tells a story or anecdote: the persuader's own experience, or a narrative about a specific child or person helped.
criteria.other: Anything else: unclear or non-English text, insults, fragments, or messages that fit none of the above.
criteria.react_to_commitment: A short appreciative reaction (great, wonderful, that will help so much) right after the persuadee explicitly agrees or pledges to donate, or names the amount they will give; it expresses gratitude for that commitment even without the word thanks.
criteria.react_to_good_deed: An approving reaction to the persuadee's own good deeds, habits, values or attitude (they volunteer, donate, care for others, say children deserve help, show they care); it credits the persuadee rather than the charity.
criteria.react_side_topic: A comment, opinion, or reaction about a side topic unrelated to the charity or donating (a celebrity, the weather, the persuadee's unrelated plans or day).
criteria.comment_positive_reaction: A short reaction to or agreement with what the persuadee said (that's great, wow, glad to hear, they are wonderful, yes that is true), including agreeing with a feeling or view the persuadee just expressed, without new information or persuasion.
criteria.persuader_musing: The persuader voices a personal remark or opinion that does not argue for donating to this charity: about governments, society, volunteering in general, or the persuader's own volunteering and side activities; often after the chat has wrapped up.
